tools.fire-calculator.faqs.0.question: What is the FIRE movement?
tools.fire-calculator.faqs.0.answer: FIRE (Financial Independence, Retire Early) is a movement focused on retiring before the traditional retirement age through aggressive saving and investing. A typical goal is accumulating 25 times your annual expenses in net worth.
tools.fire-calculator.faqs.1.question: What is the 4% rule?
tools.fire-calculator.faqs.1.answer: The 4% rule suggests you can withdraw 4% of your portfolio in the first year of retirement, then adjust that amount for inflation each year, with a very low probability of running out of money. 25 times your annual expenses achieves this.
tools.fire-calculator.faqs.2.question: How much do I need to FIRE?
tools.fire-calculator.faqs.2.answer: Multiply your annual expenses by 25. If you spend $40,000 per year, you need $1 million (40,000 × 25). This assumes a 4% safe withdrawal rate based on historical market returns.
tools.fire-calculator.faqs.3.question: What is the difference between Lean FIRE and Fat FIRE?
tools.fire-calculator.faqs.3.answer: Lean FIRE targets minimal expenses (typically under $40,000 per year), requiring less savings but a tighter budget. Fat FIRE targets luxurious spending (over $100,000 per year), requiring a larger portfolio ($2.5 million+).

tools.vat-calculator.faqs.0.question: What is VAT?
tools.vat-calculator.faqs.0.answer: VAT (Value Added Tax) is a consumption tax levied on the value added to goods or services at each stage of the supply chain. It is ultimately borne by the end consumer, and businesses remit it to the government.
tools.vat-calculator.faqs.1.question: How do I calculate the gross price from a net price?
tools.vat-calculator.faqs.1.answer: Gross price = Net price × (1 + VAT rate). If the net price is $100 and VAT is 20%: gross price = 100 × 1.20 = $120.
tools.vat-calculator.faqs.2.question: How do I extract the net price from a gross price?
tools.vat-calculator.faqs.2.answer: Net price = Gross price ÷ (1 + VAT rate). If the gross price is $120 and VAT is 20%: net price = 120 ÷ 1.20 = $100.
tools.vat-calculator.faqs.3.question: What is the difference between VAT and GST?
tools.vat-calculator.faqs.3.answer: GST (Goods and Services Tax) is a single-stage tax collected at the point of final sale. VAT is a multi-stage tax collected at each stage of the supply chain, with credits along the way. Both function similarly but differ in structure.

tools.break-even-calculator.faqs.0.answe: The break-even point is where total revenue equals total costs - no profit and no loss. Above it, the business is profitable; below it, the business loses money.
tools.break-even-calculator.faqs.1.quest: How do I calculate the break-even point (in units)?
tools.break-even-calculator.faqs.1.answe: Break-even units = Fixed costs ÷ (Selling price - Variable cost per unit). If fixed costs are $10,000, the selling price is $50, and variable costs are $30: break-even = 10,000 ÷ (50 - 30) = 500 units.
tools.break-even-calculator.faqs.2.quest: What is the difference between fixed and variable costs?
tools.break-even-calculator.faqs.2.answe: Fixed costs do not change with production levels (rent, insurance, salaries). Variable costs change with production (raw materials, direct labor, shipping). Identifying both is essential for an accurate break-even analysis.
tools.break-even-calculator.faqs.3.answe: It tells you how much you need to sell to start making a profit, informing pricing, cost control, and business planning. It helps evaluate the viability of new products or the impact of changes on profitability.

What debt-to-income (DTI) ratios do lenders use?

Most lenders prefer the 28/36 rule - housing costs at no more than 28% of gross income and total debt (including housing) at no more than 36%. Some loans allow DTI up to 43-50%, but they carry more risk.
Should I budget for home maintenance?

Yes. The rule of thumb is 1-3% of the home's value per year. A $300,000 home should have $3,000-$9,000 budgeted annually for maintenance - HVAC, roof, plumbing, and more. This is not in the mortgage payment but is essential.

The 28/36 rule suggests your housing expenses (principal, interest, taxes, insurance) should not exceed 28% of your monthly gross income, and total debt payments (housing + car loans + credit cards, etc.) should not exceed 36%.
How do property taxes and insurance affect affordability?

They have a significant impact. A $125,000 home pays $1,250 per year in property tax in a 1% state, versus $3,125 in a 2.5% state. This changes what you can afford. Always include taxes and insurance before calculating your home price.

tools.apr-calculator.faqs.0.question: What is APR?
tools.apr-calculator.faqs.0.answer: APR (Annual Percentage Rate) is the true annual cost of a loan expressed as a rate. It includes the interest rate plus fees (origination fees, closing costs, etc.), providing a single comparable number.
tools.apr-calculator.faqs.1.question: What is the difference between APR and the interest rate?
tools.apr-calculator.faqs.1.answer: The interest rate is your cost of borrowing. APR includes the interest rate plus loan fees (origination fees, points, mortgage insurance, closing costs). APR is always equal to or higher than the interest rate and gives the full cost picture.
tools.apr-calculator.faqs.2.question: Why is APR important for comparing loans?
tools.apr-calculator.faqs.2.answer: Lenders may offer a low rate with high fees, or a high rate with low fees. APR combines both into one number, making different loan products from different lenders truly comparable.
tools.apr-calculator.faqs.3.question: Does APR account for early repayment?
tools.apr-calculator.faqs.3.answer: No. APR assumes you hold the loan for its full term. If you pay off early or refinance, the actual cost may be higher because you pay the same fees over a shorter period.

tools.capital-gains-tax-calculator.metad: Calculate capital gains tax on investments, distinguishing short-term and long-term rates.
tools.capital-gains-tax-calculator.keywo: long term capital gains tax calculator
What is the difference between short-term and long-term capital gains?

Short-term gains apply to assets held for less than a year and are taxed at ordinary income rates (10-37%). Long-term gains apply to assets held for more than a year and are taxed at lower rates (0%, 15%, or 20%).
What is the Net Investment Income Tax (NIIT)?
NIIT is an additional 3.8% tax on investment income for high earners (over $200,000 single, $250,000 married filing jointly). It is added on top of regular capital gains tax.
How do capital gains interact with my other income?

Capital gains stack on top of your ordinary income. If your total income pushes you into a higher bracket, your gains may face a higher rate. Long-term gains have their own brackets, which may differ from ordinary income.
Can I offset gains with capital losses?

Yes. Capital losses first offset gains of the same type (short-term against short-term, long-term against long-term). Net losses can offset up to $3,000 of ordinary income. Excess losses carry forward to future years.

tools.gpa-calculator.faqs.0.question: How is GPA calculated?
tools.gpa-calculator.faqs.0.answer: GPA = total quality points ÷ total credits. Quality points = credits × grade points for each course. A = 4.0, B = 3.0, C = 2.0, D = 1.0, F = 0. Plus/minus adjustments: A- = 3.7, B+ = 3.3, and so on.
tools.gpa-calculator.faqs.1.question: What is the difference between weighted and unweighted GPA?
tools.gpa-calculator.faqs.1.answer: Unweighted GPA measures all courses on a 4.0 scale. Weighted GPA assigns higher values (typically a 5.0 scale) to honors, AP, or IB courses, recognizing course difficulty. Colleges may use either or both in admissions.
tools.gpa-calculator.faqs.2.question: What is a good GPA?
tools.gpa-calculator.faqs.2.answer: An unweighted 3.0-3.4 is considered good, while 3.5+ is very competitive. Weighted GPA varies by school profile. Top universities typically expect weighted GPAs above 4.0 (due to honors courses).
tools.gpa-calculator.faqs.3.question: How can I improve my GPA?
tools.gpa-calculator.faqs.3.answer: Focus on high-scoring courses to raise your cumulative GPA. Retake low-grade courses (if allowed). Balance challenging courses with ones you can do well in. Discuss strategies with your advisor.

tools.grade-calculator.faqs.0.question: How do I calculate my class grade?
tools.grade-calculator.faqs.0.answer: Multiply each category's score by its weight, then add them up. For example: Tests (50%) = 85 × 0.50 = 42.5, Homework (30%) = 90 × 0.30 = 27, Quizzes (20%) = 80 × 0.20 = 16. Total = 85.5%.
tools.grade-calculator.faqs.1.question: What score do I need to get an A?
tools.grade-calculator.faqs.1.answer: Subtract your current weighted total from the grade you want (90% for an A), then divide by the weight of the remaining category. If you have 80% and the final is worth 20%: (90 - 80) ÷ 0.20 = 50%. You need to score 50% on the final.
tools.grade-calculator.faqs.2.question: What is the difference between weighted and unweighted grades?
tools.grade-calculator.faqs.2.answer: Weighted grades account for the percentage value of each assignment and category weights. Unweighted is simply the total score divided by the total possible. Weighted is more accurate because different assignments have different importance.
tools.grade-calculator.faqs.3.question: How does dropping the lowest score affect my grade?
tools.grade-calculator.faqs.3.answer: Dropping the lowest score usually raises your grade, especially if it is significantly below your average. It works by removing the outlier that drags your average down. Calculate with and without the drop to see the difference.

tools.character-counter.faqs.0.answer: Words are counted by splitting the text on whitespace (spaces, tabs, newlines). Multiple consecutive spaces count as a single separator. Empty text has 0 words.
tools.character-counter.faqs.1.question: Which social media character limits does it track?
tools.character-counter.faqs.1.answer: Twitter/X (280), Instagram bios (150), LinkedIn posts (3,000), YouTube titles (100), TikTok captions (2,200), SEO meta titles (60), and meta descriptions (160).
tools.character-counter.faqs.2.question: How is reading time calculated?
tools.character-counter.faqs.2.answer: Based on an average reading speed of 200 words per minute. Speaking time uses 130 words per minute (average speaking pace).
tools.character-counter.labels.placehold: Type or paste your text here...
tools.character-counter.description: Count characters, words, sentences, paragraphs, and lines. Social media character limits and reading time.
tools.character-counter.guide.whatIs.bod: Count characters, words, sentences, paragraphs, and lines in any text. It also shows reading time, speaking time, and character limits for popular social media platforms.
tools.character-counter.guide.howTo.titl: How to Use the Character Counter
tools.character-counter.guide.howTo.item: Type or paste your text in the input area.
View live counts of characters, words, sentences, paragraphs, and lines.
See social media character limits in the panel below.
Check reading and speaking time estimates.
tools.character-counter.guide.tips.title: Tips
tools.character-counter.guide.tips.items: Use the no-spaces count for platforms that exclude spaces.
The tool works with any language and Unicode text.
Watch the limits for Twitter/X, Instagram bios, and meta descriptions.
tools.text-repeater.metadata.title: Text Repeater
tools.text-repeater.metadata.description: Repeat any text multiple times with a custom separator.
tools.text-repeater.faqs.0.question: What is this tool used for?
tools.text-repeater.faqs.0.answer: Repeat any text, word, or phrase a specified number of times. Useful for testing, filling form fields, social media, generating test data, or creating patterns.
tools.text-repeater.faqs.1.question: Is there a limit on the number of repeats?
tools.text-repeater.faqs.1.answer: To prevent browser lag, the tool is limited to 10,000 repeats. That is more than enough for most use cases.
